The Tokyo range window [00:00,09:00) UTC overlaps the London-morning decision window by 1-2 bars (BST: 07:00Z+08:00Z; GMT: 08:00Z). A decision bar that is part of its own T_H/T_L can never strictly breach (self-referential extreme), so the effective trigger window is 2-3 bars, not '4 hourly bars', and is DST-asymmetric. Not a lookahead (bar completed before entry), but a specification defect the implementation must resolve deterministically (exclude decision bar from range or accept dead bars).
Cross-cutting X2 applies: Monday Tokyo ranges are complete only via convention-out-of-session Monday 00:00Z bars, and then span the weekend gap; the spec does not pin the bar universe.
Fold F1 nominally starts 2020-03-01 but the compression state first becomes evaluable 2020-03-04/05; fail-closed absorbs the 3-4 day misalignment.
Weekly governor binds in 85 pair-weeks (9 signals dropped, not deferred) — compliant, but not 'not expected to bind' as the proposal states.

findings.finding: BLOCKING: the forced-flat fallback ('exit fills at the first available later H1 bar open the same UTC day') is unsatisfiable whenever the 16:00 NY bar is missing on a Friday. Measured: all 36 flat-bar-missing leg events (2.7% of 1,346 legs) occurred on provider-short Fridays (e.g. Fridays ending 13:00Z), where no later bar exists the same UTC day. The frozen spec therefore has NO defined exit for those legs: the only outcomes are forbidden weekend carry (carry is FORBIDDEN per frequency_contract) or an undefined/crashing schedule. As written the proposal cannot be implemented deterministically under the no-carry contract.

Frequency claims optimistic: gate incidence 38.9% vs claimed 50-70%; construction cadence 1.99 RT/week vs ~3.0 claimed; per-pair 0.29/week vs 0.86 claimed. Cell floors still clear (204/218/251 RT per fold >= 100; decisions 1,734 >= 250), so feasibility is unaffected, but the estimates should not be relied on downstream.
